title: A common room can never be used in a prison that has a yard, and a kitchen can never be used at all
body:
Two rooms a player can build, complete and pay for, which no prisoner will ever use. Both measured over an 18-day played run with three prisoners, 346 prisoner-observations.

## The common room loses to the yard in every state that occurs

`action.yard-recreation` (`src/simulation/prisoners/actions.ts:88`) names **no** `requiredObjectCapability`, so its concurrent-use ceiling is `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` (`src/simulation/prisoners/room-instance-registry.ts:350`) and a zoned yard always resolves.

`scoreAction` (`src/simulation/prisoners/utility-ai.ts:16-24`) then scores:

- yard: `recreation × 3 + safety × 0.1`
- common room: `recreation × 2`

and every regime block that admits one admits the other — both are `category: 'recreation'` (`src/simulation/prisoners/regime.ts:110,113,115`, plus the high-risk and riot sets).

The only state in which the common room wins is `recreation === safety === 255` **exactly**.

Measured: a finished common room from day 14; over days 15–18, 120 prisoner-observations, `action.yard-recreation` 22 performing / 8 travelling, and `action.common-room-recreation` **zero across the entire run**.

A yard costs nothing to build — an 8×8 of open ground, no walls, no materials, no money. The common room in that run cost 19 wall segments and two benches.

## The kitchen has no action at all

Walled, zoned and furnished with a stove, prep counter and fridge; the panel then reports nothing outstanding. **No entry in `DEFAULT_ACTIONS` targets `room.kitchen`**, and nothing else under `src/` reads it — a grep excluding the catalogue and the buildable rows returns nothing. No prisoner went near it in 346 observations.

That run spent 15 wall segments and three objects on it. Nothing misbehaves; nothing happens either, and nothing on screen says so.

## Related, and measured on the same run

Separately worth recording: `eat_meal` was observed 5 performing / 4 idle / 9 travelling, while `eat-in-cell` ran 11/2/1 — and every user of a room stands on its **anchor tile**, so a whole canteen of diners occupies one tile.

## Scope

Both of these are **balance and content**, not defects in the mechanism — which under `AGENTS.md`'s standing mandate makes them the owner's call, not an agent's. Filed as a measurement so the decision rests on numbers rather than on impression. There are three plausible readings and they lead to different work: the yard is too strong, the common room needs a reason to exist that the yard cannot serve, or the kitchen needs an action before it should be buildable at all.
